verdict.rationale: OpenClaw is self-hosted by design. The Gateway runs on your own machine or container, memory is plain Markdown in a local workspace (default ~/.openclaw/workspace), and session history is SQLite in per-agent state directories, so the user decides where core data lives by choosing the host. Users can also choose their LLM provider, including local models, which affects where prompts are processed. However, nothing in the docs explicitly addresses residency, and conversations still pass through third-party chat channels and any remote LLM provider the user selects. Missing for 10: explicit data-residency/region documentation, guidance on data flows to chat platforms and LLM providers, configurable workspace/state location documented as a residency control, independent corroboration.
